subject: Communication
title: Teaching EQ: Can Schools Change Hearts?
description: Learn Teaching EQ: Can Schools Change Hearts? in one minute.

hook.text: A school in New Haven taught emotional literacy. Suspensions dropped 50%. Test scores rose.

buildup.text: Social-Emotional Learning (SEL) programs teach children to identify emotions, manage them, show empathy, and navigate conflict.

discovery.text: A meta-analysis of 213 studies showed SEL programs improve academic achievement by 11 percentile points and reduce misconduct.

twist.text: Critics worry SEL is 'soft' or distracts from academics. Data shows the opposite: emotional skills boost cognitive performance.

climax.text: Countries like Singapore, Finland, and Australia now embed EQ into their national curricula.

punchline.text: The most important subject in school might be understanding yourself.

quiz.question: By how many percentile points does SEL improve academic achievement?

details.summary: Social-emotional learning programs in schools teach children to recognize emotions, manage impulses, show empathy, and build relationships. Meta-analyses show SEL programs improve academic performance by 11 percentile points and reduce behavioral problems. The evidence is strong and growing.
details.whyItMatters: Teaching EQ in schools is one of the most cost-effective educational investments available, improving both social skills and academic outcomes simultaneously.
takeaways: SEL programs improve academic performance by 11 percentile points
They reduce behavioral problems and improve social skills
The evidence for school-based EQ programs is strong

faq.question: What do social-emotional learning programs actually teach?
faq.answer: Core skills include self-awareness, self-management, social awareness, relationship skills, and responsible decision-making. Programs use role-playing, discussion, journaling, and mindfulness exercises. They are integrated into the school day rather than added as separate classes.

faq.question: Are critics right that schools should focus on academics, not emotions?
faq.answer: The evidence shows this is a false choice. SEL programs improve academic performance because students who can manage emotions focus better, collaborate more effectively, and persist through challenges. Emotional skills and academic skills reinforce each other rather than competing.
